# Compliance audit: brief vs. repository (HEAD 96b3dd0, audited 2026-11-21)

I read the brief with `pdftotext` (4 pages). Nothing was edited.

## 1. Requirements table

| # | Brief requirement (page) | Status | Evidence / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl" (p1) | MET | run.py:280-303. Extra flags are optional and the defaults are the submitted config. |
| 2 | Read every video in the Parquet files; "mp4 column holds the video file as bytes" (p1-2) | MET | vidx/source.py:21-56 reads row by row, handles a null mp4 or unreadable row group and keeps going. |
| 3 | `video` = "Parquet file name without its folder, a colon, and the row number… from 0" (p2) | MET | source.py:30,54. If the whole parquet cannot be opened, there is a single `<file>:0` error line (row count unknown). That is reasonable. |
| 4 | Second N = timestamp ≥N and <N+1, "counted from the first decoded frame" (p2) | MET | decode.py:53-75 (first pts becomes 0, exact Fraction), aggregate.py:236 |
| 5 | "line for every second up to and including the second that holds the last frame"; empty second → `[]`, `"people": 0` (p2) | MET | aggregate.py:240-243. Sampling keeps at least 1 frame per second (sampling.py:284), so no second is lost. |
| 6 | Object names exactly as in §1 (p2) | MET | aggregate.py:4 |
| 7 | Error line with an `error` field; partial failure keeps earlier lines plus one error line (p2) | MET | run.py:164-172, pipeline.py:119-121, sampling.py:308-311 |
| 8 | "Keep going if a video is damaged" (p1) | MET, with risk | Decode and source errors become error lines. The inference-failure abort (exit 3) is a risk, see R1. |
| 9 | Present if found in "at least half" of frames; median "rounded down" at .5 (p2) | MET | aggregate.py:16-24,249. This is applied to the 3 sampled frames, not to all frames. |
| 10 | YOLO11l, official `yolo11l.pt`, input 640, conf ≥0.4 (p2) | MET | model.py:9-10; prepare.py downloads the official asset |
| 11 | "Keep the Ultralytics defaults for everything else: letterbox…, class-aware NMS IoU 0.7, BGR" (p2) | MET / UNCLEAR | Uses the Ultralytics `LetterBox(auto=True)` with the predictor's own args (iou 0.7, agnostic False), model.py:146-207. BGR input is converted to RGB exactly as the predictor does. The FP16 and `classes=` filter questions are in R2/R3. |
| 12 | "If a video has a rotation tag, rotate its frames" (p2) | MET in code, NOT VERIFIED | decode.py:105-143. The sign convention matches ffmpeg autorotate by my reading, but the worklog Pending list still has the rotation check open (WORKLOG:40). |
| 13 | Accuracy: F1 ≥0.95, exact ≥85%, ±1 ≥95% (p2) | MET on own refs | README:16-17. Tune 0.988/0.959/0.999, holdout 0.990/0.968/0.999. |
| 14 | Python 3.11, CUDA 12 driver, RTX 4090 (p3) | MET, partly unverified | torch 2.6.0+cu126 installed cleanly on 3.11 (WORKLOG #9). It was never run on a 4090. |
| 15 | "pip install -r requirements.txt" (p3) | MET | requirements.txt has `--extra-index-url` cu126 |
| 16 | "list the sudo apt-get install commands in your README" (p3) | PARTIAL | README:50 has no `sudo apt-get update` first. On a fresh VM, install can fail with "Unable to locate package". |
| 17 | Preparation command: "download yolo11l.pt" (p3) | MET | README:55-59, prepare.py |
| 18 | Timed run "without internet access" (p3) | MET in code, NOT VERIFIED | model.py:97-106 (YOLO_OFFLINE, sync=False). The offline test is still pending (WORKLOG:10,44). |
| 19 | "Some test files may be damaged or unusual" (p3) | PARTIAL | Handled in code, but the damaged-input test is still pending (WORKLOG:43). |
| 20 | "stop any run that takes longer than 6 hours" (p3) | MET | Measured 125 h on an L4 in 1 h 52 min. 13 h of test video should take minutes. |
| 21 | run.py + code files (p3) | MET | run.py, vidx/ |
| 22 | requirements.txt: "Every Python package your script needs, with exact versions" (p3) | PARTIAL | Only direct deps are pinned. Transitive deps from ultralytics (matplotlib, pandas, scipy, psutil, ultralytics-thop…) float. Lines 2-3 still say "PROVISIONAL: these pins are not yet verified". |
| 23 | README: "exact steps to install and run… apt-get… preparation command" (p3) | MET except #16 | README:48-64 |
| 24 | results.jsonl.gz: "results for all 50 files" (p3) | MET | 461,757 lines, 1,650 videos, 50 files (00000–00049), 0 errors. Code changed since tag results-v1 only in a stats line (run.py:461-462), so the results still match the code. |
| 25 | HARDWARE.md: GPU and memory, CPU model and cores, RAM, "disk type (SSD or hard disk)", "operating system", total time (p3) | PARTIAL | **Operating system is missing.** Disk type says "Colab local disk", not SSD or HDD. Everything else is present. |
| 26 | WRITEUP.md: answers to §8 (p3-4) | NOT YET DONE | The file does not exist. |
| 27 | ai_chats/: full, unedited chats; tokens → `[REMOVED]`; Claude Code `.jsonl` from `~/.claude/projects/`; web share links in `links.txt` (p3) | NOT YET DONE | Only links.txt (comments) is there. No `.jsonl` copied. |
| 28 | Deadline: "Sunday 22 November 2026, 11:55 pm… last commit" (p1) | Pending | Today is 21 Nov. The working tree has an uncommitted WORKLOG.md. |
| 29 | "write-up answers must be your own words, written without AI" (p1, p4) | User's task | Not audited by design |

## 2. BLOCKERS (fix before the deadline)
1. **WRITEUP.md is missing.** The brief lists six questions (p4). Headings only, with no content suggested:
   1. "Your timings." (100 words)
   2. "Your pipeline." (150)
   3. "Where the time goes." (150)
   4. "Checking correctness." (100)
   5. "Working with AI." (100)
   6. "Next steps." (100)

   The brief adds: "we stop reading at the limit."
2. **ai_chats/ is missing the Claude Code logs.** `~/.claude/projects/D--video-indexing-yolo11/` has two sessions (`6cf43f45….jsonl` 3.5 MB, `c229ec4a….jsonl` 4.6 MB). Each also has a folder with `subagents/*.jsonl` (8.6 MB and 4.1 MB). Copy all of them, since the brief says "full" and "A missing or edited history counts against you". Copy last so the current session is complete.
   - I scanned for `hf_…`, `ghp_`, `sk-` and `github_pat_`. The only hit is this audit's own regex text, so it is a false positive. Re-scan just before pushing.
   - Add share links for any web chats (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Gemini, Colab Gemini) to links.txt.
3. **HARDWARE.md:** add the operating system (Colab's Ubuntu version) and the disk type (SSD), both named explicitly in the brief.

## 3. RISKS / AMBIGUITIES
- **R1, abort on inference failure** (run.py:479-483). Three failed batches in a row exit with code 3, and the pending videos plus everything after them get no lines. The grader runs once, so missing videos would likely count against accuracy. Fix: for the plain grader command, write error lines and keep going (or reload the model, or drop to batch 1) instead of exiting. The same applies to `RuntimeError("all decode threads failed")` and a re-raised `source_exc` (pipeline.py:224-227), which end the whole run.
- **R2, FP16.** The brief says "Keep the Ultralytics defaults for everything else", and Ultralytics' default is `half=False`.
  - The brief's examples (letterbox, NMS, BGR) are about geometry and post-processing, not precision. "Make it as fast as you can while keeping the results correct" plus tolerance thresholds suggests approximation is acceptable.
  - Still, this is ambiguous. The brief invites questions: "reply to the email that sent you this brief, before the deadline." Consider asking, and note it in the write-up (the user's decision is already logged in the WORKLOG).
- **R3, sampling 3 frames/s.** The brief neither forbids nor allows it. The grading text ("Make it as fast as you can while keeping the results correct", thresholds below 100%, "A simple version can be written in an afternoon. There is a lot of room to make it faster") implies approximations are expected. Low risk. Note that the margin on unseen data is not huge: 0.959–0.968 exact against a bar of 0.85, which is fine.
- **R4, the `classes=[0,2,16,63,67]` filter** is a non-default predict argument. With class-aware NMS it gives the same output unless a frame has more than 300 detections (max_det); the worklog says "classes filter vs none identical". Negligible, but it is a deviation from defaults.
- **R5, direct inference that bypasses `predict()`, and cross-video batching.** The brief says nothing about it. It uses Ultralytics' own LetterBox, backend, NMS and args, and the worklog reports results identical to `predict()` on 1,000 frames. Low risk.
- **R6, unverified grader-path checks** (the worklog Pending list): offline run, damaged mp4 and corrupt parquet, rotation sign. All three are "MET in code" only. If rotation is wrong, rotated phone clips in the test set would be scored with the wrong orientation.
- **R7, `requirements.txt`.** Remove the "PROVISIONAL" comment (install was verified on 3.11 per WORKLOG #9). Consider pinning the full set from `pip freeze` in the Colab 3.11 venv to match "every Python package… exact versions".
- **R8, `apt-get update`** missing before the install (see #16).
- **R9.** The 4090 / CUDA 12 driver combination was never tested. The cu126 wheels need a driver of at least 525 (12.x minor-version compatibility), so it should be fine.
- **R10, the brief PDF is gitignored.** That is fine, nothing requires it.

## 4. NOT YET DONE
- WRITEUP.md, written by the user without AI.
- ai_chats/ with all `.jsonl` files (sessions plus subagents) and web links.
- HARDWARE.md: operating system and disk type.
- README: `sudo apt-get update`. requirements.txt: drop "PROVISIONAL" and optionally pin the full freeze.
- Grader-path checks: offline run, damaged input, rotation.
- Commit the WORKLOG.md change, run the final secret scan (`git grep -nE "hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"` plus the ai_chats folder), and push before 22 Nov 23:55 PKT.

## 3. RISKS / AMBIGUITIES
- **R1, abort on inference failure** (run.py:479-483). Three failed batches in a row exit with code 3, and the pending videos plus everything after them get no lines. The grader runs once, so missing videos would likely count against accuracy. Fix: for the plain grader command, write error lines and keep going (or reload the model, or drop to batch 1) instead of exiting. The same applies to `RuntimeError("all decode threads failed")` and a re-raised `source_exc` (pipeline.py:224-227), which end the whole run.
- **R2, FP16.** The brief says "Keep the Ultralytics defaults for everything else", and Ultralytics' default is `half=False`.
  - The brief's examples (letterbox, NMS, BGR) are about geometry and post-processing, not precision. "Make it as fast as you can while keeping the results correct" plus tolerance thresholds suggests approximation is acceptable.
  - Still, this is ambiguous. The brief invites questions: "reply to the email that sent you this brief, before the deadline." Consider asking, and note it in the write-up (the user's decision is already logged in the WORKLOG).
- **R3, sampling 3 frames/s.** The brief neither forbids nor allows it. The grading text ("Make it as fast as you can while keeping the results correct", thresholds below 100%, "A simple version can be written in an afternoon. There is a lot of room to make it faster") implies approximations are expected. Low risk. Note that the margin on unseen data is not huge: 0.959–0.968 exact against a bar of 0.85, which is fine.
- **R4, the `classes=[0,2,16,63,67]` filter** is a non-default predict argument. With class-aware NMS it gives the same output unless a frame has more than 300 detections (max_det); the worklog says "classes filter vs none identical". Negligible, but it is a deviation from defaults.
- **R5, direct inference that bypasses `predict()`, and cross-video batching.** The brief says nothing about it. It uses Ultralytics' own LetterBox, backend, NMS and args, and the worklog reports results identical to `predict()` on 1,000 frames. Low risk.
- **R6, unverified grader-path checks** (the worklog Pending list): offline run, damaged mp4 and corrupt parquet, rotation sign. All three are "MET in code" only. If rotation is wrong, rotated phone clips in the test set would be scored with the wrong orientation.
- **R7, `requirements.txt`.** Remove the "PROVISIONAL" comment (install was verified on 3.11 per WORKLOG #9). Consider pinning the full set from `pip freeze` in the Colab 3.11 venv to match "every Python package… exact versions".
- **R8, `apt-get update`** missing before the install (see #16).
- **R9.** The 4090 / CUDA 12 driver combination was never tested. The cu126 wheels need a driver of at least 525 (12.x minor-version compatibility), so it should be fine.
